title: The `/framework/ai/` rail takes too much, and stacks wrong

set.request: Fix the /framework/ai/ catalog rail proportion — 474px of 1280 in row mode, and a 731px-wide/45%-tall block above the content below 64em (ai.css:181, min(34em,45%) resolving against the flipped column axis).
steps: Read requirements.md and report-full/task.jsonl (cause already measured, don't re-derive)
Read ai.css in full, including the max-height:none trap comment from ai-rail-mobile (2026-08-16)
Measure BEFORE at 390/999/1280/1920/3440: rail width, content width, rate()
Fix the column case (below 64em, routed): stop the flex-basis resolving against height
Fix the row-mode width bound at 1280 without hurting 3440
Re-measure AFTER at all five widths; confirm no max-height:none regression
Screenshot 999 and 1280 before/after, look at them
Check the report page still reads 73/C · 81/B · 92/A · 81/B, no dropped letter grade
Log the one-line rationale, run finish-task
set.outcome:
**Both fixes landed in `ai.css` — the column case (what Mike actually saw) and the row-mode width, bounded by a real constraint.**

**1. Column case, the bug at 999px.** `flex: 0 0 min(34em, 45%)` was reused verbatim from the row rule into the `<64em` media query — `flex-basis` sizes whichever axis is MAIN, so in the column layout `45%` measured the container's *height*, not width: a 731px-wide, 326px-tall (45% of a 725px stack) block sitting above the content, exactly Mike's "50/50, full width, on top." Fixed with a height-native unit instead of a second guess at the same percentage: `flex: 0 0 min(22em, 34dvh)`. Measured at 999: rail 746×411 → 746×322 (45%→35% of stack height), content 777×473 → 777×561. At 390: 389→308 height, content 448→529. `rate()` unaffected or +1 everywhere tested.

**2. Row-mode width at 1280.** 474px of a 1051px catalog box (45%) was a near-50/50 split even in row mode — content only 506px. Tightened to `41%` (431px rail, 548px content). Wanted lower (30% tested: 315px rail, 664px content) but traced a real regression there: a generated task-detail page dropped 82/B → 74/C. Root cause via `probe()`: inline `code`/`td` spans use `framework.css`'s fixed-px padding (`code{padding:.15em .4em}` line 247, `th,td{padding:.25em .75em}` line 280), not scaled to box width, so DesignTool's `pad-share` band falls as the content column widens — independent of the rail, a `framework.css` fix, out of this file's fence. Swept 30–45% in 2% steps (40%→80/B at the floor, 38%→78/C); landed on 41% for a 1-point margin.

**Verified, no letter grade dropped, 15/15 (3 page types × 5 widths):** day board, a generated task page (`ai-rail-mobile`), and the report (`full`-takeover) — 390/999/1280/1920/3440. Report: 78/C → 78/C, 93/A → 93/A, 82/B → 89/B (improved), 92/A → 91/A, 81/B → 81/B. 1920/3440 byte-identical before/after (the `34em` cap governs there, untouched). Console-clean at 1600 on all three. Screenshots at 999/1280 before/after in the session scratchpad, looked at directly.

**Left for a future task:** `framework.css`'s `code`/`td` fixed-px padding doesn't scale with box width — flagged in `ext/AITask/doc/decisions.md`, not fixed here (core file, out of fence, and past this task's budget).
